subject: botany
question_text: Mention a single membrane bound organelle which is rich in hydrolytic enzymes.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The organelle
lines: It is a tiny sac bound by a single membrane,
and it is formed by the Golgi complex.
steps.why: The question gives two clues — one membrane, and hydrolytic enzymes — and only the lysosome matches both.
common_mistakes: Answering mitochondrion or chloroplast. Both have two membranes.
Answering ribosome. A ribosome has no membrane at all.
steps.memory_tip: Lyso comes from lysis, which means splitting. A lysosome splits things apart.
steps.margin_note: The single word Lysosome earns this mark.

steps.label: Its enzymes

lines.text: Lysosome = single membrane sac of hydrolases

lines: It is rich in hydrolytic enzymes — lipases,
These enzymes work best in an acid medium.
steps.why: Hydrolytic means the enzyme splits a bond by adding water, so naming the classes of hydrolase is what shows you know the word in the question.
common_mistakes: Writing that lysosomal enzymes work in an alkaline medium. They need an acid medium.
Naming no enzyme class at all.
steps.memory_tip: Four food types, four enzyme jobs: carbohydrate, protein, lipid, nucleic acid.
steps.margin_note: Name the acid medium and two enzyme classes.

insider_note: One word is the whole answer, but a bare 'lysosome' usually earns only half the marks — add the acid medium and the enzyme classes.
